matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        }\n    }\n\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n\n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A;\n    }\n\n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n\n    if (validate) {\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", valid ? \"PASSED\" : \"FAILED\");\n        return valid ? 0 : 1;\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

The work is complete — here's a summary.\n\n## What I did\n\nParallelized `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` with MPI using a **pipelined fan-out Cholesky with cyclic row distribution**, and updated `CMakeLists.txt` to require and link MPI (`find_package(MPI REQUIRED)`, `MPI::MPI_CXX`). The executable name is unchanged and the program now always runs under MPI (single rank works too).\n\n**How it's parallelized:**\n- Rows are distributed cyclically (rank `r` owns rows `i` with `i % nprocs == r`), which keeps the shrinking trailing workload balanced across ranks throughout the factorization.\n- At step `j`, row `j` of L is broadcast and every rank computes element `(i, j)` for its owned rows `i > j` — the O(n³/3) work is evenly split.\n- **Lookahead pipelining:** the owner of row `j+1` finishes that row first and starts a non-blocking `MPI_Ibcast` of it, so the broadcast overlaps with everyone's remaining step-`j` updates instead of serializing on the critical path.\n- Matrix generation (`A = B·Bᵀ`, also O(n³)) and validation (`L·Lᵀ` reconstruction) are parallelized over owned rows as well; validation errors are combined with an `MPI_MAX` reduction.\n\n**Bit-exact semantics:** since the result hash in `print_results` is a byte-level FNV hash, I kept every element's computation identical to the original — same left-looking dot products in the same summation order — only the schedule and location of the work changed. The non-positive-definite error path is preserved (owner prints the same message, all ranks return failure consistently).\n\n## Verification\n\n- Hashes are **bit-identical** to a freshly built copy of the original sequential code for n=5, 293, 512, 2000 at 1, 2, 3, 4, and 8 ranks (including ranks > n), and `-v` validation passes everywhere.\n- `-h`, unknown-option, and failure exit codes behave as before.\n- Scaling on this machine, n=2000: 1991 ms (1 rank) → 537 ms (4) → 209 ms (16) → 139 ms (64). n=4096: 16.7 GFLOPS (16 ranks) → 40.4 GFLOPS (128 ranks). Per-core throughput is bounded by the sequential-order dot products (a bit-exactness requirement the original shares), so scaling headroom on a real cluster is primarily the per-step broadcast, which the Ibcast lookahead hides.\n\nOne note: the existing `build/` directory contained a stale CMake cache from a different path, so I cleared it and reconfigured before building."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":323,"cache_read_input_tokens":43301,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":323},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"afe852a7-a4d4-4879-9377-c96c9cbeb695","uuid":"31568439-b417-4eed-96ee-51ce6eaf60fc","timestamp":"2026-09-04T01:09:25.787Z","request_id":"req_011CehWHTQ836zcGs3FwzaAa"}

Per-core throughput is bounded by the sequential-order dot products (a bit-exactness requirement the original shares), so scaling headroom on a real cluster is primarily the per-step broadcast, which the Ibcast lookahead hides.\n\nOne note: the existing `build/` directory contained a stale CMake cache from a different path, so I cleared it and reconfigured before building.","ttft_ms":3613,"ttft_stream_ms":2941,"time_to_request_ms":69,"type":"result","duration_ms":541286,"uuid":"3bb962b0-9801-4303-bfe4-62b0c6ec5850","queued_turn_count":0}
